detailed_summary.v3.overview: The video gives a one-bowl, no-cook meal aimed at people trying to gain weight or muscle. It combines 40 g rolled oats, 200 g curd, one medium banana, five pitted dates and a handful of unsalted roasted peanuts. The oats are soaked directly in curd, then topped with banana, dates and peanuts. The creator describes the meal as roughly 700-plus calories with around 20 g protein and suggests using it once daily, often between meals or a few hours before training. Peanut allergy substitutions include almonds, cashews or walnuts, and plant-based yogurt is suggested for vegans. The most useful principle is that weight gain requires a sustained calorie surplus; resistance training helps direct some of that gain toward muscle rather than only fat. The exact promised speed of visible results is not established and calorie needs should be individualized.

title_en.v1.title: Healthy Weight-Gain Foods: Milk Dalia, Curd-Potato, Banana-Peanut Butter, Roti-Rice, Paneer and Urad Dal
title_en.v1.reason: These calorie-dense foods and combinations are explicitly detailed.

detailed_summary.v3.overview: The video argues against relying on sugary commercial mass gainers and instead recommends calorie-dense whole-food combinations. It gives detailed recipes for milk dalia or milk-oats with dry fruit, curd with boiled potatoes, and a banana-peanut-butter smoothie made with water. It also recommends eating roti and rice together at lunch, using paneer and legumes for protein, particularly black urad dal, and combining increased calorie intake with resistance training rather than only eating more. A sample day includes milk dalia or paneer/paratha at breakfast, roti plus rice with legumes at lunch, a banana-peanut-butter smoothie or sattu/dry-fruit laddus as snacks, a lighter roti-sabzi or dal-rice dinner, and milk at night. The broad principles—calorie surplus, protein adequacy, resistance training and sleep—are useful. Ayurvedic claims about food combinations slowing metabolism, Ashwagandha causing weight gain, extra water improving heavy-food digestion and guaranteed 15-day changes are not established.

detailed_summary.v3.overview: The video lays out a detailed vegetarian day for weight gain and muscle building. Morning starts with water, optional sesame-oil massage and a banana mixed with ghee and jaggery before training. Post-workout whey is suggested. Breakfast is broken-wheat cashew upma cooked with ghee, chana dal and vegetables. Snack is seasonal fruit. Lunch combines whole-wheat chapatis, semi-brown rice, black-chana curry and lassi. The evening snack is a roti spread with two tablespoons peanut butter and wrapped around a banana. Dinner includes rice, chapati, paneer curry and whole urad dal. Before bed, the creator prepares milk with Ashwagandha, cardamom, turmeric, pepper, ghee and crushed nuts. The practical value is high because recipes and meal timing are concrete. The strongest evidence-aligned principles are adequate energy/protein and resistance training; traditional claims about massage, meal combinations, eating with hands and Ashwagandha should be treated cautiously.
